articles.title: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
articles.full_text:
Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt. 

This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have its “ChatGPT moment” — that day when the shockingly capable chatbot was launched in late 2022. (General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte told Equity earlier this year that a single general foundation model would make much of today’s specialized robotics work redundant, and be that moment.) 

On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis caught up with Vishwanath to discuss where she’s writing first checks as the founder and managing partner of Techable VC. They also talked about what she’s learned as one of the first women executives to spin out of Nvidia and launch her own early-stage firm investing in physical AI across robotics, materials science, and life sciences.

articles.summary:
Former NVIDIA robotics product marketing lead Amulya Vishwanath argues robotics remains in a foundational "Lego era," pushing back against predictions of an imminent "ChatGPT moment" driven by a single general foundation model. Now founder and managing partner of Techable VC, she shared her investment thesis and lessons from spinning out of NVIDIA on the Equity podcast.

  • Core view: Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA's robotics platforms, says the industry's basic building blocks—actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards—are still being rebuilt, meaning robotics is far from a breakthrough moment.
  • Counterpoint: Her assessment challenges voices like General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte, who has argued that a single general foundation model would render much of today's specialized robotics work redundant and trigger a ChatGPT-style leap.
  • New venture: As founder and managing partner of Techable VC, Vishwanath is writing first checks in physical AI across robotics, materials science, and life sciences.
  • Background and impact: She is one of the first women executives to spin out of NVIDIA and launch an early-stage firm, and she discussed those lessons with host Dominic-Madori Davis on TechCrunch's Equity podcast.
